texts.facts: Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (Pfa Act), wherein it is alleged that the accused persons had sold misbranded food in violation of Section 2 (ix)(k) of PFA Act read with Rule 32(e) of PFA Rules, as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act. In Re vs A-1) Raj Kumar Goel on 7 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19966618/ 1 2. As per the complaint, on 25.05.2009, the food officials including Food Inspector (FI) O. P. S. Ahalwat and Field Assistant (FA) Ashok Kumar under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. Bhupinder Singh reached at the premises of M/s. In & Out, Yashwant Place Service Station, Africa Avenue, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi-110021, where the accused no. 1 in the capacity of vendor-cum-partner of M/s. Yashwant Place Service Station was found vending "Moong Washed Dal Split" in sealed packets of 500 grams each, having identical label declaration. The food officials lifted the sample the said food article consisting of three such sealed packets ready for sale for human consumption. It was divided into three parts as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules and separately packed and sealed. Necessary documents were prepared at the spot including the vendor's receipt and panchanama. One counterpart of the sample was deposited with the Public Analyst (PA) and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 06.06.2009, the PA reported that the article was conforming to the standards, yet the sample was found misbranded being in violation of Rule 32(e) of PFA Rules, because there was no batch number / code number declared on the label. Based on the report of PA, investigation was carried out by the Food Inspector as per the instructions of the SDM/LHA. It was found that the accused no. 3 business concern M/s. Yashwant Place Service Station was a partnership firm, of which accused no. 1 and 2 were the partners. Further, the sample article was manufactured and supplied by accused no. 4 being the proprietor of M/s. Sunny Enterprises. Hence, after obtaining due sanction of the Director, PFA, the present complaint came to be filed against all the accused persons for violation of the section 2(ix)(k) read with Rules 32(e), as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act. 3. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused persons were summoned vide order dated 20.01.2010. Based on the report of PA, notice of accusation under section 251 CrPC was framed against all the accused persons for commission of offence under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act, vide order dated 27.04.2010, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 4. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 Sh. Bhupinder Singh (SDM/LHA), PW-2 FI O. P. S. Ahalawat and PW-3 FA Ashok Kumar were the part of the team that had visited the premises of accused no. 3 and lifted the sample of "Moong Washed Dal Split" from accused no. 1 vendor, as lying in sealed packets of 500 grams each. These witnesses deposed about the sample proceedings conducted by them on 25.05.2009 and narrated the steps undertaken by them, including disclosing their identity, lifting three sealed packets, dividing the same in three counterparts by considering one sealed packet as one counterpart and separately packing them. A sum of Rs. 120/- was paid to the vendor as price of the sample vide vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A. Notice in Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B was prepared upon which the vendor disclosed that the food article had been purchased from accused no. 4. Accordingly, a notice under section 14A of PFA Act Ex. PW-1/B-1 was prepared. Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C was also prepared and the accused issued cash memo Ex. PW-1/D while also handing over a copy of the invoice Mark-X showing purchase of commodity from accused no. 4. The Raid Report Ex. PW-2/A was prepared at the spot. On the next working day, one counterpart was deposited with the PA vide receipt Ex. PW-2/B and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA vide receipt Ex. PW-1/E. PA report Ex. PW-1/F was received opining the sample to be misbranded. Further investigation was carried out by PW-2 In Re vs A-1) Raj Kumar Goel on 7 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19966618/ 2 during which various letters were written to ascertain the constitution of the business concerns involved. Consent for prosecution Ex. PW-1/G was taken from the Director, PFA, after which the complaint Ex. PW-1/H was filed and intimation letter Ex. PW-1/I was sent to the accused vide postal receipt Ex. PW-2/E. The witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld. Defence Counsel, wherein they denied that the accused persons had been falsely implicated. 5. Statements of the accused persons were recorded under section 313 CrPC on 20.12.2014 wherein they denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. They questioned the correctness of PA report and claimed that the present is a false case. No defence evidence was however led by them.
texts.arguments: 6. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to prove its case against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt, as all the witnesses have supported its case and there is no condition in their testimony. It is submitted that the accused has failed to rebut the findings as given by the PA. 7. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel has submitted that the prosecution case fails on various grounds. Ld. Counsel has submitted that Rule 32(e) has already been declared ultra vires of the Constitution by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the judgement titled as Dwarka Nath v. MCD [1972 FAC 1 (SC)] and that no prosecution can lie under this provision against the accused persons. Further, it is submitted that there are various contradictions in the testimony of the witnesses which would falsify the prosecution case. 34. As far as Rule 32(e) is concerned, the defence has relied upon the judgement titled as Dwarka Nath v. MCD (supra) wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India had struck down the said provision being beyond the rule making power under section 23(1) of the PFA Act. 36. In view of this factual position, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that: In Re vs A-1) Raj Kumar Goel on 7 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19966618/ 9 It is submitted that against the said judgement of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, the State went in appeal before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as NCT of Delhi v. Mohinder Singh [Criminal Appeal no. 1470/11] and vide order dated 27.08.2015, the Hon'ble Supreme Court reiterated that since Rule 32(e) of PFA Act had already been declared ultra vires of the constitution, no case could lie in the matter. 19. For that matter, even the order dated 27.08.2015 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as NCT of Delhi v. Mohinder Singh [Criminal Appeal no. 1470/2011] would not be applicable, because that order also pertained to a sample lifted on 23.08.1993 (copy of the pleadings to this effect has been shown by the Ld. Defence Counsel).
